question: An $\alpha$-particle of kinetic energy $6.0\text{ MeV}$ approaches a silver nucleus head-on. Calculate the distance of closest approach. Take $Z=47$, $e=1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ and $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^2\text{ C}^{-2}$.

options.A: $r_0\approx4.6\times10^{-14}\text{ m}$ because gold and silver have the same nuclear charge.
options.B: $r_0\approx1.15\times10^{-14}\text{ m}$ because only one electron charge is used.
options.C: $r_0\approx2.3\times10^{-13}\text{ m}$ because the kinetic energy is $9.6\times10^{-14}\text{ J}$.
options.D: $K=6.0\times10^6\times1.6\times10^{-19}=9.6\times10^{-13}\text{ J}$. For a head-on approach, $r_0=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{2Ze^2}{K}$, so for $Z=47$, $r_0\approx2.3\times10^{-14}\text{ m}$.
